purpose: Freeze only publicly observable morphology statements that may guide later visualization comparison of a delivered velocity(x,y,z,t) field. This file is not a numeric fit target and is not PDE evidence.

source.title: On the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
source.evidence_scope: Public prose and figure caption only; no hidden velocity samples, coefficients, camera metadata, or source data are asserted.

observables.public_observation: The displayed motion is described as a rotating vortex or swirl.
Displayed trajectories stretch or elongate along the vortex axis.
The central region is described as shrinking while its speed increases.
The public rendering distinguishes regions of faster and slower angular rotation.
Circulating speed is described as depending on radius.

unknown_or_unrecoverable_from_public_dis: absolute spatial scale and coordinate registration
color transfer function and rendering normalization
allowed_downstream_use: Use the observable IDs as qualitative labels in a separately preregistered candidate comparison.
Derive autonomous numerical diagnostics only after recording their definitions, sample sets, and thresholds separately from this source contract.
Keep visual/morphology evidence independent from PDE acceptance.
forbidden_inferences: Treating a pixel or color match as recovery of the hidden OpenAI velocity field.
Inferring exact camera, coordinates, coefficients, pressure, forcing, or time mapping from the public display.
Promoting qualitative visual agreement to Navier-Stokes residual acceptance.
Retuning a candidate on held-out visual evidence and then calling that same evidence independent validation.

external_method_screening.license: BSD-3-Clause (project default; individual vendored files may differ)
external_method_screening.candidate_scope: image segmentation, morphology, feature extraction, and optical-flow style tooling for future public-frame diagnostics
external_method_screening.reason: A pixel-space objective is premature without a frozen public frame, camera/projection model, color mapping, and frame-to-time registration. Adopting it now would create styling-specific numerical targets rather than source-supported velocity constraints.
